message.content: The description model is already in place, and the two open claims (c1 truncation, c2 fp32 rounding) lack evidence. I'll add a targeted update guiding evidence collection: because the matrix is exactly Q·diag(λ)·Q^T with a Hadamard Q, the iteration's modal decomposition is analytically exact, so a CPU-side fp64/fp32 simulation of the 64-step loop is decisive evidence without needing the GPU.

Q^T b = b_modal is computable on CPU deterministically, so per-mode error analysis (b_i/λ_i)(1-λ_i)^64 needs no GPU.", "Because Q is a Hadamard matrix, |b_modal_i| are exact linear combinations of the fp32 rhs entries with coefficients ±0.25; they are NOT necessarily uniform (~0.25 each) — the specific seed 701010 rhs must be projected to get the actual weights, which decides claim c1.", "Kernel computes state += rhs - A state; per-step this is Richardson with unit step size, error mode i multiplied by exactly (1-λ_i) in exact arithmetic; 0.03125 -> factor 0.96875, 0.96875^64 ≈ 0.129.", "enable_fp_fusion=False means residual and state update are separately rounded fp32 ops (no FMA contraction); tl.sum over 16 terms is a fp32 reduction whose order is compiler-determined but deterministic."], "open_questions": ["Actual modal weights b_modal = Q^T rhs (fp32 rhs, fp64 projection) for seed 701010 — this single vector decides c1's estimated ~0.11 vs the 0.08 bound.", "Whether the CPU fp32 simulation and the Triton kernel agree bit-for-bit (tl.sum reduction order vs torch dot); Expected per-mode residual factor (1-λ)^64: 0.96875^64≈0.129 (λ=0.03125), 0.9375^64≈0.016 (λ=0.0625), negligible for the rest.", "Decisive evidence path for c2: CPU fp32 simulation of the same 64-step loop (simulating kernel arithmetic) compared to the fp64 simulation; separates rounding from truncation. message.reasoning_content: The claims c1 and c2 lack evidence; description model already recorded. No open description tasks. I can add a refinement to the description model clarifying evidence needs for the skeptics' claims — e.g., precise quantitative decomposition, noting matrix stored in eigenbasis Hadamard so error analysis is exactly per-mode; also note matrix entries exact in fp32? Q entries ±1/4, eigenvalues chosen so A entries are sums of λ_i/16 — fp32 rounding of matrix may slightly perturb eigenvalues, but negligible. Also note the exact spectral decomposition enables deterministic CPU simulation of the fp64 64-step iteration, and error after 64 steps: state = (I-(I-A)^64) A^{-1} b... Actually a key point: exact per-mode factor for truncation: (1-λ)^64. Could also note skeptic's estimate can be validated analytically since b_i = Q^T b are computable. Record a small update to open_questions/risk_map guiding experimenters: a CPU fp64 simulation of the iteration gives decisive truncation error, and fp32 simulation approximates rounding.
